clue.text: Hail diminished, but it's still bleak

parts.note: to hail someone is to acclaim or applaud them, to give them a cheer
diminished means reduced, made smaller: less

explanation.surface: Even after the hailstorm eases off, the weather remains grim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like weather; it is the verb meaning to acclaim, and 'diminished' is the adjective 'less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bleak is joyless and gloomy, lacking any warmth or comfort.

clue.text: Charm poet with your first, exotic picture in colour

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign-looking, so these letters take on an unfamiliar new order
first asks for the opening letter of the word your

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to captivate a poet, along with a striking coloured painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges CHARM, POET and Y, the first letter of 'your'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chromatype is a photographic print or process producing an image in colour, using chromium salts.

clue.text: He may put out the last champion

indicators.note: the last of the word the means its final letter only

parts.note: a champion is the winner of a contest, a victor

explanation.surface: Someone may be eliminating the reigning title-holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last' looks like a description of the champion; it is the final letter of 'the', E.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who evicts a tenant puts that person out of the property.

clue.text: Meal out on the river, for the department

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece written on another sits above it, so the river letter comes first

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of meal are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Dining out on a river boat, as part of some organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece written 'on' another sits above it, so the river comes first; 'department' means a sphere of activity, not an office.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a sphere or domain of activity, much as a department is a field of responsibility.

clue.text: Acquires personal knowledge of exciting, epic sex with rené

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters of these words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named René has a thrilling romantic encounter and learns about life first-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience something is to undergo it yourself and so learn about it first-hand.

clue.text: In chess, irrational move trapped knight

indicators.note: trapped means held inside, so the answer is caught within the words chess, irrational move

explanation.surface: At the chessboard, a wild, illogical move left a knight cornered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped' finds the answer inside 'chesS IRrational'; the chess knight is a decoy for the title given to a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the title placed before the name of a knight, so it can stand for one.

clue.text: Convincing evidence, though may need amending

explanation.surface: Solid evidence is offered, even though it might need some changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a printer's trial sheet, which an editor corrects before final printing.
explanation.definitionFit: Conclusive evidence establishes a fact, and a printer's trial impression is checked and corrected before publication.

clue.text: Fish first seen at river, that's plain

parts.note: the pike is a large freshwater fish

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word seen

parts.note: the Taff is a river in South Wales that flows through Cardiff

explanation.surface: An angler first spots a fish by the river and finds the matter obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the saying 'as plain as a pikestaff', meaning perfectly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikestaff is the proverbial example of something obvious, from the idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff'.

clue.text: Ring leading expert about lines to superintend

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pair of letters goes round the lines

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: leading means at the front, so the opening letter of expert is taken

parts.note: lines of poetry are verse

explanation.surface: A gang boss and a leading specialist come together to supervise operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring leading' looks like a ringleader; O and E (the first letter of 'expert') are wrapped 'about' VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or watch over work, which is what superintending means.

clue.text: Can't move quickly

explanation.surface: Someone is unable to get anywhere at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one idea, but splits into two senses: stuck fast, and moving fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held fast is firmly fixed and immovable, while running fast means at speed.

clue.text: Academician is a Russian lady

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London

explanation.surface: A member of an academy is said to be a woman from Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword staple for an artist; Raisa Gorbachev was a famous Russian bearer of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisa is a Russian woman's given name, as borne by Raisa Gorbacheva, wife of the last Soviet leader.

clue.text: Birds a rat keeps worrying

indicators.note: worrying means harassing or shaking about, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A pet rodent is pestering some caged birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Parakeets are small long-tailed parrots, a kind of bird.

clue.text: Promise Thomas unusual change of form

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters are taken out of their ordinary order

explanation.surface: A man called Thomas is promised a remarkable transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: A metamorphosis is a transformation, like a caterpillar becoming a butterfly.

clue.text: Pilots cheer wildly, to be in them?

definitions.text: Pilots cheer wildly, to be in them?

indicators.note: wildly means in an unrestrained way, so the letters of these words are flung into a new order

explanation.surface: Aviators applaud with enthusiasm at the prospect of being aboard rotary aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: aircraft that pilots would be glad to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Helicopters are rotor-driven aircraft that pilots sit in and fly.

clue.text: Seeks information about heading off from duties for a game of golf

indicators.note: heading off means the head, the first letter, is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: duties are tasks
a round is one complete game of golf over the course

explanation.surface: Someone makes enquiries about skipping work to play eighteen holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off from' removes the first letter of the synonym for duties; 'about' and 'for' are only links in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask around is to enquire of several people in search of facts.

clue.text: English net returns cover mistake of a mundane character

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it, so the reversed letters enclose the mistake
returns means comes back, so the two letters for English and net are read backwards together

parts.note: net is taken as written
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: An English goal-net keeps returning to hide a blunder by a dull player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses E and NET as one run, giving TENE, and 'cover' wraps that round the mistake; 'mundane' here means earthly rather than dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrene means earthly or worldly, as opposed to heavenly or spiritual.

clue.text: Flashing of the shoulder by English girl

parts.note: Paulette is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An English girl is flashing her shoulder at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flashing' here is a noun for a trim or ornamental strip, not exposure.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is the ornamental shoulder piece on a military uniform, a decorative strip on the shoulder.

clue.text: Casual shoes put out for sale

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or disrupted, so these letters are disrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: Some relaxed slip-on footwear is put on display to be sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like 'displayed' but it rearranges FOR SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loafers are slip-on leather shoes without laces, worn informally.

clue.text: A crop is knocked flat

indicators.note: knocked means battered about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A field of grain has been flattened by the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like the crop's state; it means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means dull and unimaginative, just as flat writing lacks interest.

clue.text: Remark in words that may appear to be verbose

indicators.note: may appear to be suggests a disguise, so the letters of verbose take on another arrangement

explanation.surface: A comment phrased in a way that seems long-winded.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer, rearranged, can look like 'verbose'.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to remark or comment, as in observing that it looks like rain.

clue.text: Many presents in these boxes

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
to present something is to offer it

explanation.surface: Lots of gifts are kept inside these chests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' looks like gifts but is the verb 'offers'; 'Many' gives C, the Roman hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are strongboxes in which money or valuables are kept.

clue.text: Necessitates quarters being provided for dogs

parts.note: east and north are two of the four quarters of the compass, giving E and N
to dog someone is to follow them closely, to tail them

explanation.surface: Housing has to be supplied for canine pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings; it is two compass points. 'dogs' is a verb meaning follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to require it as a consequence, to make it necessary.

clue.text: With fish, drink black-malt ale? There's only one of us in favour

definitions.text: only one of us in favour

parts.note: the sole is a flatfish
to sup is to drink in sips
porter is a dark beer brewed from roasted black malt

explanation.surface: At dinner over fish and dark beer, one diner finds themselves alone in backing a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTER is a dark British beer, close cousin of stout.
explanation.definitionFit: A sole supporter is the single person who backs something, with nobody else in agreement.

clue.text: Took a picture featuring this creature

indicators.note: featuring means including or containing, so the answer is contained within the words took a picture

explanation.surface: A photographer snapped an image with an animal in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring' finds the answer in 'tOOK A PIcture'.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a shy African mammal related to the giraffe, a striking animal.

clue.text: Cleft sticks hold them?

indicators.note: hold means contain, so the answer is contained within the words cleft sticks

explanation.surface: Do forked twigs trap little creatures?
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' finds the answer in 'clEFT Sticks'; the whole clue doubles as a picture of the newts being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Efts are young newts, small amphibians one might pin with a forked stick.

clue.text: Capital to take the initial levy

parts.note: initial means coming at the start, first
a rate is a local tax or levy

explanation.surface: A city is planning to impose its first tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city; it is the exclamation meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital as an old-fashioned exclamation or adjective means excellent, top-notch.

clue.text: Give more, to become a theologian

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a degree held by a theologian

explanation.surface: Contribute further in order to qualify as a scholar of religion.
explanation.walkthrough: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, an advanced degree in theology.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to supply something extra, to put in more.

clue.text: Farewell to the French!

parts.note: a goodbye word borrowed from French, literally meaning 'to God' in that language

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to the people of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is the French goodbye, and literally means 'to God'.
explanation.definitionFit: This goodbye was borrowed from French and is used in English to bid someone a final parting.

clue.text: Is rejecting first mate's riddle?

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the word is is turned backwards

parts.note: Eve was Adam's mate in Genesis

explanation.surface: Is the first spouse's puzzle being turned down?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns IS into SI, which comes 'first'; 'riddle' is a coarse sieve, not a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a large coarse sifting tool used to separate soil or grain from stones.

clue.text: Spurned, second girl passed on, outside

indicators.note: outside means around, so the word for passed on goes round the other letters

parts.note: to pass on is a euphemism for to die
a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Rejected, a second girl walked by, staying out in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed on' looks like walked past; it is the euphemism DIED, placed 'outside' S and MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dismissed is to be rejected or brushed aside, as a spurned idea is.
